chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever does not pray with the Imam in congregation on the day of Eid, there is no prayer (Salaat) for him and no make-up (Qaza) is obligatory upon him.

key_terms.یَوْمَ الْعِیدِ: Eid day (the day of the festival prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up the Eid prayer if missed?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Eid prayer is a congregational obligation (Jama'ah) tied to the presence of the Imam; thus, missing it without a valid excuse results in no compensatory make-up (Qaza) prayer. This ruling underscores the unique status of Eid Salaat as a communal act of worship rather than a simple individual duty, reflecting the Shia emphasis on unity and leadership in religious observances. The absence of Qaza highlights that the primary purpose—communal gathering with the Imam—was not fulfilled, distinguishing it from daily obligatory prayers.
